tools.name: ask_people
tools.description: Opens a call: one short task to several people. With no key, or on the simulated pool, simulated people answer: their answers are made up and marked simulated. Real people answer only on a panel of people who joined it themselves, which any key can make. Returns a call_id at once; ask_people_results

tools.name: ask_people_cancel
tools.description: Stops a call. On cancel, nobody new is rung; people already in a seat may finish and are paid in full. Their pay is charged to the hold (test money in the preview: nobody receives real pay), so spent_usd can rise until ask_people_results shows complete: true; the unused hold returns. Returns the cal

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: ask_people_quote, ask_people, ask_people_results · Private data: ask_people, ask_people_results · Public sink: ask_people, ask_people_send_outcome, ask_people_panel.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: ask_people_quote, ask_people, ask_people_results · Private data: ask_people, ask_people_results · Public sink: ask_people, ask_people_send_outcome, ask_people_panel

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "ask_people" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
